name: zone-topology-spread-cannot-move-packed-pods
description: A `ScheduleAnyway` zone topology spread does NOT spread pods that fit on existing nodes, because kube-scheduler only scores FEASIBLE nodes: if every untainted matching node is in one zone, every pod lands there and the node autoscaler is never consulted, since nothing is Pending. Use when: (1) a Deployment carrying a `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` spread is entirely in one AZ and you are about to call it a scheduler bug, (2) you are reviewing or writing a zone spread for a workload whose pods are small relative to a node, (3) you are considering `DoNotSchedule` + `minDomains` to force the spread and need to know what it costs during an AZ outage, (4) pods stay Pending for the whole duration of a zone failure and you need to know whether that is the spread, (5) a rolling update lands both new pods in one zone in a two-zone region, (6) someone calls a zone spread "AZ resilience" before checking the workload's dependencies. Covers why ScheduleAnyway is inert for packed pods, the two traps in `DoNotSchedule` + `minDomains` (`nodeTaintsPolicy` counting tainted zones, and a lost zone still counting as a domain), `matchLabelKeys` during a rollout, and the dependency check that decides whether any of it buys resilience.
author: voitta-ai
